key_terms: Geometrical meaning of zeroes: The zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the exact x-coordinates of the points where the graph of y = p(x) intersects the x-axis.
Maximum number of zeroes: A polynomial of degree n can intersect the x-axis at most n times, thus possessing at most n zeroes.
Parabolic graph of quadratic polynomials: Graphs of y = ax^2 + bx + c form parabolas opening upwards if a > 0 or downwards if a < 0.
Relationship between zeroes and coefficients of quadratic polynomials: For ax^2 + bx + c with zeroes alpha and beta, alpha + beta = -b/a and alpha * beta = c/a.

Relationship between zeroes and coefficients of cubic polynomials: For ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d with zeroes alpha, beta, gamma, sum of zeroes = -b/a, sum of pairwise products = c/a, and product of zeroes = -d/a.
